text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Suspicious log egress detected from staging cluster 'stg-west-2'. Pattern: multiple small PUTs to an external S3 endpoint (s3://suspicious-bucket-xyz) from svcacct-staging-logshipper. Confidence score 0.87. Paging @oncall-marc for triage.
oncall-marc: ack — looking.

sec-alyssa: @oncall-marc starting triage. Any evidence keys/tokens were included in payloads? Can you pull the last 1h of PUT requests and sample objects?
oncall-marc: grabbing logs now, running query.

infra-raz: I see identical user-agent 'log-forwarder/1.2.3' hitting a single external host 13.23.45.67 over 443. Not in our known destinations list — probably misconfigured sink or compromised pipeline.

oncall-marc: here's sanitized tail of nat-proxy logs:
```
PUT https://13.23.45.67/obj1 ... svcacct-staging-logshipper
PUT https://13.23.45.67/obj2 ... svcacct-staging-logshipper
```

sec-alyssa: thanks. Is this forwarder supposed to talk to external buckets? Raz can you confirm bucket owner and whether we have a contract?

infra-raz: reverse DNS/WHOIS shows it's not our account. I can push an immediate egress deny at the VPC ACL and add an iptables drop on the nat nodes. Proposed quick block: firewall rule 'egress-block-external-log-sink' deny to 13.23.45.67/32:443.

sre-john: agree on blocking, prefer to apply at the VPC route table / network ACL so we don't churn nat instances. @raz can you apply there?

infra-raz: applying ACL now, ETA ~30s.

incident-bot: ACTION: Applied egress ACL rule 'egress-block-external-log-sink' -> DENY 13.23.45.67/32:443 (applied_at 2026-03-17T12:07:20Z). Notifying oncall.

oncall-marc: egress blocked. Monitoring shows traffic drop; no further PUTs to that host in the last 2m.

sec-alyssa: next steps: rotate staging service principal keys for svcacct-staging-logshipper and invalidate current tokens. @infra-raz can you rotate creds and push new secrets to staging?

infra-raz: starting key rotation: creating new key in KMS, issuing new secret in Secrets Manager, will restart forwarders in a rolling fashion.

product-lee: quick question on impact: this is staging-only, right? No production tenants should be affected, but we need to confirm nothing from prod was copied into staging.

sec-alyssa: good point. @oncall-marc please grep the last 24h of files for prod markers (e.g., 'prod-account-id', 'customer_email', 'user_id'). Prioritize PII indicators.

oncall-marc: running quick grep... found 3 objects containing 'prod-account-id: 98765' plus a couple stack traces with 'user_email' fields. Looks like an automated sync job mistakenly pointed to staging. Flagging as potential customer data exposure.

legal-sam: capture a sample of retained artifacts and preserve chain-of-custody. We'll need a scoped statement if customer data is confirmed. Do not send external notices until we confirm.

sec-alyssa: containment checklist (short):
1) egress block (done)
2) key rotation for svcacct (in progress)
3) identify and delete objects from external bucket (raz + sec)
4) audit access logs and list affected files (marc)
5) verify config of any prod->staging sync jobs (eng-config)
6) determine customer impact and prepare next steps

infra-raz: contacting owner of 13.23.45.67 and their abuse contact. Also running S3 list using our ops creds — found 14 objects; issuing delete requests now.

sre-john: recommend we spin up a 20m bridge to coordinate faster. I'll create it and post the link in the bridge channel.

product-lee: drafting an internal note for CSMs: 'Investigating potential staging log leak. No confirmed customer impact; will update in 30m.'

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: incident-id 5990011223 - mitigation in progress. thread_ts 5955551234.

oncall-marc: update: key rotation complete, forwarders restarted with new creds, no PUTs to 13.23.45.67 for 10m. External object deletion progress: 8/14 deleted.

sec-alyssa: good. Next: run content scan on the 6 remaining objects and confirm deletion. Also start audit to see if any uploads contained raw tokens.

infra-raz: deletion complete for remaining objects; confirmed 14/14 deleted from external bucket (owner confirmed). Adding 13.23.45.67 to internal IP blocklist and will update firewall playbook.

legal-sam: please record affected object names + proof of deletion. I'll review for notification requirements.

product-lee: if any PII confirmed, we'll prepare a timeline + notify execs & CSMs. Keep me looped.

sec-alyssa: creating post-incident ticket and assigning owners: sec-alyssa (lead triage), infra-raz (cleanup & prevent), oncall-marc (evidence + audit), legal-sam (retention & review), eng-config (fix sync job). Reconvene on bridge in 15.

oncall-marc: last update pre-bridge: evidence collected, rotation done; no further egress activity. Marking incident as contained for now.

sec-alyssa: closing initial triage. I'll open a postmortem template with severity classification 'P2' and list remediation: tighten egress rules for staging, enforce destination allowlists, add alert for anomalous external PUTs, and require docs for any sync jobs that touch prod data.

infra-raz: will follow up with firewall rule commit and a short ops runbook change to prevent accidental prod->staging syncs.

incident-bot: Thread archived: incident-5990011223. Reminder to run /playbook incident-response-data-leak and schedule postmortem within 72h.

oncall-marc: thanks all — will post final incident summary after postmortem is populated.
